title: Voronoi L-decomposition of PSD_n and the Hypermetric Correlation Cone
relevance: Directly treats membership in the hypermetric correlation cone, equivalent to nonnegativity of the associated inhomogeneous integer quadratic form. It states membership is in co-NP and explicitly says NP-hardness was unknown (pp. 3–4). This is a useful direct status source, not prior hardness; it gives no equivalent X3C/circumsphere reduction.

title: Interior Point and Semidefinite Approaches in Combinatorial Optimization
venue: Graph Theory and Combinatorial Optimization, pp. 101–157, Springer
relevance: Potential false-positive prior-art citation: p. 33 says checking violated hypermetric inequalities is NP-hard, but supplies no reduction and cites Avis (2003) and Avis–Grishukhin (1993), whose full-problem statements say complexity is unknown. Its displayed max-cut family a^T X a >= 1 with odd sign-sum is rounded-psd under the terminology in the supplied note, so this does not establish all-gonality pure hypermetric hardness.

title: Contributions to Determining Exact Ground-States of Ising Spin-Glasses and to their Physics
relevance: Potential false-positive prior-art citation: p. 23 states that separating hypermetric inequalities is NP-hard, but gives no proof there and cites Deza–Laurent (1997); the cited chapter says the exact complexity was unknown and only smallest-violated-gonality was NP-hard. Record as an unsupported secondary assertion, not as a result that establishes arbitrary separation or an equivalent construction.

title: Cut-Polytopes, Boolean Quadric Polytopes and Nonnegative Quadratic Pseudo-Boolean Functions
authors: Boros, Endre and Hammer, Peter L.
relevance: Omitted direct predecessor cited secondhand in the note: establishes the cut/BQP/nonnegative quadratic pseudo-Boolean correspondence and reports polynomial separation for specialized large facet subclasses. Its abstract does not establish polynomial separation of the full hypermetric or Boros–Hammer families; reading the full paper would delimit the subclasses precisely.

title: Generalised 2-circulant inequalities for the max-cut problem
authors: Kaparis, Konstantinos and Letchford, Adam N. and Mourtos, Ioannis
relevance: Gives an exact O(n^5) separator for generalized and extended generalized 2-circulant facet inequalities, a structured cut-polytope family. This does not settle full hypermetric, gap-1, rounded-PSD, hypermetric-correlation, or Boros–Hammer separation, but updates the map of exact polynomially separable subclasses.

title: Solving SDP relaxations of Max-Cut problem with large number of hypermetric inequalities by L-BFGS-B
relevance: Peer-reviewed computational study that strengthens the max-cut SDP with a subset of hypermetric inequalities and explicitly uses heuristic separation. It provides solver evidence, not an exact full-class oracle or a separation-complexity result.

title: On the cut polytope
authors: Barahona, Francisco and Mahjoub, Ali Ridha
relevance: Foundational cut-polytope paper for the Barahona–Mahjoub odd-clique facets and switching operation; anchors the cut-form family attribution.

title: The Boolean quadric polytope: Some characteristics, facets and relatives
relevance: Foundational source for the Boolean quadric polytope and Padberg’s distinct clique, cut, and generalized-cut facet families; useful for keeping these separate from cut-polytope odd-clique inequalities.

title: The cut polytope and the Boolean quadric polytope
relevance: Establishes the affine congruence between the cut and Boolean quadric polytopes, which transfers facet and separation questions between the formulations.

title: Binary positive semidefinite matrices and associated integer polytopes
authors: Letchford, Adam N. and Sørensen, Michael M.
relevance: Proves separation reductions linking Boros–Hammer, hypermetric-correlation, rounded-psd, and hypermetric inequalities; records the pre-hardness open status and the equivalences among these families.

title: Complexity results for the gap inequalities for the max-cut problem
authors: Galli, Laura and Kaparis, Konstantinos and Letchford, Adam N.
relevance: States that separation for the remaining cut-polytope classes, including odd-clique inequalities and their switchings, was unknown; identifies odd clique with the Barahona–Mahjoub cut-form family and discusses its IQP formulation.

title: A new separation algorithm for the Boolean quadric and cut polytopes
authors: Letchford, Adam N. and Sørensen, Michael M.
relevance: Gives exact polynomial-time separation for specific subclasses, including odd bicycle-wheel and (2p+1,2)-circulant inequalities and switchings, using covariance and switching maps; it does not separate the full odd-clique family.

title: The Boolean Quadric Polytope
venue: The Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization Problem: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications, Springer, pp. 97–120
relevance: The latest broad status source located before the manuscript: §7.2 lists Padberg families (10)–(13) as unknown but suspected NP-hard, and the remaining cut-polytope families—including Barahona–Mahjoub odd cliques (18) and switchings—as unknown.

title: Chvatal-Gomory Rounding of Eigenvector Inequalities for QCQPs
authors: Dey, Santanu S. and Jiang, Nan and Kazachkov, Aleksandr and Lodi, Andrea and Muñoz, Gonzalo
relevance: Post-2022 work whose conic closure result identifies a subfamily with the Boros–Hammer inequalities and whose computational method generates sparse cuts; it makes no exact-separation complexity claim for the full family.

title: Minkowski's Convex Body Theorem and Integer Programming
relevance: Primary exact-CVP worst-case theorem: Theorem 4.5 (§4, p. 430) gives O(r^r s) arithmetic operations for input length s and bounds intermediate rational bit lengths by O(r²(s + log r)); the problem has a rational basis and target. This yields r^{O(r)} poly(s) bit time. Applying it to rational Gram-only input uses the same exact inner-product computations and is a representation-level inference, since the theorem states the coordinate-input model.

title: A bound on the k-gonality of facets of the hypermetric cone and related complexity problems
authors: Avis, David and Grishukhin, Viacheslav P.
relevance: Primary source for the named hypermetricity test: §4, P6 asks whether an integer metric is hypermetric and labels its complexity unknown. The paper proves co-NP membership and hardness for bounded-gonality testing/minimum violated gonality, not unrestricted hypermetricity hardness.

title: Hypermetrics in Geometry of Numbers
authors: Deza, Michel and Grishukhin, Viacheslav P. and Laurent, Monique
relevance: Primary geometric source connecting hypermetrics and L-polytopes/empty ellipsoids (§§2–3). It supports the circumsphere-membership formulation, but does not establish hardness of that test.
